s: When settlers moved onto the Great Plains of North America in the nineteenth century, they faced a serious problem.
There were very few trees, so wood for building was scarce and expensive.
paragraphs.zh: 十九世紀拓荒者遷入北美大平原時，面臨一個嚴重的問題：那裡樹木很少，建屋用的木材稀少又昂貴。

s: Their solution was to build with the ground itself.
They cut thick blocks of sod, soil held together by grass roots, and stacked them like bricks.
paragraphs.zh: 他們的解決辦法是直接用土地本身蓋房子。他們切下厚厚的草皮塊——由草根緊緊抓住的泥土——像磚塊一樣堆疊起來。

s: These sod houses had clear advantages.
Their thick walls kept them warm in winter and cool in summer, and they rarely burned.
paragraphs.zh: 這種草皮屋有明顯的優點。厚牆使屋內冬暖夏涼，而且很少著火。

s: However, they also leaked during heavy rain, and insects often lived in the walls.
As railroads made lumber cheaper, most families replaced them with wooden homes.
paragraphs.zh: 不過，下大雨時會漏水，牆裡也常住著昆蟲。隨著鐵路使木材變便宜，大多數家庭都改住木屋。

glossary.en: a person who goes to live in a new area
a way to solve a problem
a layer of soil with grass growing in it
to put things on top of each other
to let water in through a hole

mcq.zh: 樹木很少，木材稀少又昂貴。
mcq.en: There were few trees, so wood was scarce and expensive.

mcq.en: Their thick walls kept them warm in winter.

mcq.en: "Scarce" means hard to find.

options: The government paid them to move
mcq.en: Railroads made lumber cheaper.

tf.s: Sod houses often caught fire.

s: Corn, or maize, is one of the most important crops in the world, yet it does not grow wild anywhere.
For a long time, its origin puzzled scientists.
paragraphs.zh: 玉米是世界上最重要的作物之一，但它在任何地方都不會野生生長。長久以來，它的起源令科學家困惑。

s: Genetic studies have now shown that maize developed from a wild grass called teosinte, which grows in southern Mexico.
Teosinte looks very different from modern corn.
paragraphs.zh: 基因研究現已證實，玉米是由一種生長在墨西哥南部、名叫大芻草的野草演變而來。大芻草的樣子和現代玉米很不一樣。

s: Its ears are tiny and hold only about a dozen hard seeds.
Over thousands of years, farmers kept seeds from the plants with the largest and softest ears.
paragraphs.zh: 它的穗很小，只有十幾顆堅硬的種子。數千年來，農民一直保留穗最大、最軟的植株的種子。

s: This careful selection began around nine thousand years ago.
Slowly, it turned a wild grass into a crop that now feeds billions.
paragraphs.zh: 這種細心的選種大約從九千年前開始，慢慢把一種野草變成了今天養活數十億人的作物。

glossary.en: to make someone unable to understand
the part of a grain plant that holds the seeds

mcq.q: What is unusual about maize?
options: It does not grow wild anywhere
mcq.zh: 它在任何地方都不會野生生長。
mcq.en: It does not grow wild anywhere.

mcq.q: What did genetic studies show?
options: Maize came from a wild grass
mcq.zh: 玉米由野草大芻草演變而來。
mcq.en: Maize developed from a wild grass, teosinte.

mcq.q: How is teosinte described?
options: It has small ears with hard seeds
It is a kind of tree
mcq.zh: 穗很小，只有十幾顆堅硬的種子。
mcq.en: Its ears are tiny and hold about a dozen hard seeds.

mcq.q: According to the passage, how did farmers change the plant?
options: By keeping seeds from plants with the best ears
mcq.zh: 保留穗最大、最軟的植株的種子。
mcq.en: They kept seeds from the plants with the largest and softest ears.

mcq.q: The word "puzzled" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
mcq.en: "Puzzled" means confused.

tf.s: Teosinte grows in southern Mexico.
The change from teosinte to maize happened in a few years.
tf.en: False: it took thousands of years.

tf.s: Maize now feeds billions of people.

title.text: The Long Journey of the Monarch

s: Every autumn, millions of monarch butterflies leave Canada and the northern United States and fly south to central Mexico.
Some travel more than four thousand kilometers.
paragraphs.zh: 每年秋天，數百萬隻帝王斑蝶離開加拿大和美國北部，向南飛到墨西哥中部。有些飛行超過四千公里。

s: What makes this journey remarkable is that no single butterfly has made it before.
The monarchs that fly south are the great-grandchildren of those that left Mexico the previous spring.
paragraphs.zh: 這趟旅程令人驚奇之處在於：沒有一隻蝴蝶曾經飛過這條路。往南飛的帝王斑蝶，是前一年春天離開墨西哥那批蝴蝶的曾孫輩。

s: Scientists believe the butterflies use the position of the sun to find their direction.
An internal clock lets them adjust for the sun's movement across the sky.
paragraphs.zh: 科學家認為，蝴蝶是靠太陽的位置來辨別方向。體內的生理時鐘讓牠們能依太陽在天空中的移動來調整。

s: In recent decades, their numbers have fallen sharply, mainly because the milkweed plants their young depend on are disappearing.
paragraphs.zh: 近幾十年來，牠們的數量大幅減少，主要是因為幼蟲賴以為生的馬利筋植物正在消失。

mcq.q: Where do the monarchs fly in autumn?
mcq.en: South to central Mexico.

mcq.q: What makes the journey remarkable?
options: No butterfly has made the journey before
The journey takes only a week
mcq.zh: 沒有一隻蝴蝶曾經飛過這條路。
mcq.en: No single butterfly has made it before.

mcq.q: According to the passage, how do monarchs probably find their direction?
options: By using the position of the sun
mcq.zh: 靠太陽的位置辨別方向。
mcq.en: They use the position of the sun.

mcq.q: Why have monarch numbers fallen?
mcq.zh: 幼蟲依賴的馬利筋正在消失。
mcq.en: The milkweed plants their young depend on are disappearing.

mcq.q: The word "remarkable" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
mcq.en: "Remarkable" means surprising.

tf.s: Some monarchs fly more than four thousand kilometers.
The same butterflies return to Mexico every year.

tf.en: False: the ones flying south are the great-grandchildren.

tf.s: Young monarchs depend on milkweed plants.
tf.en: True: their young depend on milkweed.

s: On a summer evening, the center of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the countryside around it.
This effect is known as an urban heat island.
paragraphs.zh: 夏天傍晚，大城市的市中心可能比周圍鄉村熱上好幾度。這種現象稱為「都市熱島」。

s: The main cause is the materials cities are built from.
Asphalt and concrete absorb heat during the day and release it slowly after sunset.
paragraphs.zh: 主要原因在於城市的建材。柏油和混凝土白天吸收熱量，日落後再慢慢釋放出來。

s: In addition, cities have fewer trees, which cool the air by releasing water through their leaves.
Air conditioners and cars add even more heat.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，城市的樹木比較少，而樹木會透過葉子釋出水分來使空氣降溫。冷氣機和汽車又帶來更多熱量。

s: To reduce the problem, some cities are planting trees, painting roofs white and creating rooftop gardens.
paragraphs.zh: 為了減輕這個問題，有些城市正在種樹、把屋頂漆成白色，並打造屋頂花園。

glossary.en: a black material used on roads
on the top of a building

mcq.q: According to the passage, what is an urban heat island?
options: A city that is warmer than the area around it
A hot island near a city
A park in the city center
mcq.zh: 市中心比周圍鄉村熱好幾度。
mcq.en: A city center several degrees warmer than the countryside around it.

mcq.q: What do asphalt and concrete do?
options: Absorb heat and release it slowly

mcq.en: They absorb heat during the day and release it slowly.

mcq.q: How do trees cool the air?
options: By releasing water through their leaves
mcq.en: By releasing water through their leaves.

mcq.en: Building more roads is not mentioned.

mcq.en: "Release" means let out.

tf.s: City centers can be several degrees warmer than the countryside.
Cars and air conditioners help cool cities.
tf.en: False: they add even more heat.

tf.s: Cities usually have more trees than the countryside.

s: Before coins existed, people traded goods directly or used objects such as shells and grain as money.
These systems worked, but they had limits.
paragraphs.zh: 在錢幣出現以前，人們直接以物易物，或用貝殼、穀物等物品當作錢。這些方法行得通，但有其限制。

s: Grain could spoil, and it was hard to agree on the value of a cow compared with a pot.
paragraphs.zh: 穀物會腐壞，而且一頭牛和一個陶罐各值多少，也很難談妥。

s: The first true coins appeared in Lydia, in what is now Turkey, around 2,600 years ago.
They were made of electrum, a natural mixture of gold and silver, and stamped with an official mark.
paragraphs.zh: 最早真正的錢幣大約在兩千六百年前出現於呂底亞，也就是今天的土耳其一帶。它們以琥珀金——一種天然的金銀混合物——製成，並蓋上官方印記。

s: The mark guaranteed the coin's weight, so people no longer needed to weigh metal at every sale.
Trade became faster, and the idea soon spread to Greece and beyond.
paragraphs.zh: 這個印記保證了錢幣的重量，人們不必再在每次買賣時秤量金屬。交易變得更快，這個點子很快就傳到希臘及更遠的地方。

glossary.en: seeds of plants like wheat and rice
to promise that something is true

mcq.q: What did people use as money before coins?
mcq.zh: 用貝殼、穀物等物品當錢。
mcq.en: Objects such as shells and grain.

mcq.q: What was one problem with using grain as money?
mcq.en: Grain could spoil.

mcq.q: According to the passage, where did the first true coins appear?
mcq.zh: 出現於呂底亞（今土耳其）。
mcq.en: In Lydia, in what is now Turkey.

mcq.q: Why was the official mark important?
mcq.zh: 印記保證了錢幣的重量。
mcq.en: The mark guaranteed the coin's weight.

mcq.q: The word "spoil" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
mcq.en: "Spoil" means go bad.

tf.s: The first coins were made of pure gold.
tf.zh: ×：琥珀金，是天然的金銀混合物。
tf.en: False: electrum, a mixture of gold and silver.

tf.s: Lydia was in what is now Turkey.
Coins made trade faster.

title.zh: 為什麼臨時抱佛腳沒用

s: Many students study by reading the same material again and again the night before a test.
This feels effective, but research suggests it is one of the least efficient ways to learn.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學生的讀書方式，是在考試前一晚反覆讀同樣的內容。這感覺很有效，但研究顯示，這是最沒效率的學習方法之一。

s: In the 1880s, the German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus found that people quickly forget new information unless they review it.
He also found that reviews spread over several days work far better than one long session.
paragraphs.zh: 1880 年代，德國心理學家艾賓浩斯發現，新資訊若不複習，人們很快就會忘記。他也發現，分散在幾天內的複習，效果遠比一次長時間的學習好。

s: This is called the spacing effect.
Each time we recall something after a delay, the memory becomes stronger and lasts longer.
paragraphs.zh: 這叫做「間隔效應」。每次隔一段時間再回想某件事，記憶就會更牢固、維持得更久。

s: Many language apps now use this idea, showing each word again just before the learner is likely to forget it.
paragraphs.zh: 現在許多語言學習 app 都運用這個概念，在學習者快要忘記某個單字之前，再讓它出現一次。

glossary.en: a scientist who studies the mind
a period of time for an activity

mcq.q: What is true of rereading the night before a test?
options: It feels effective but is inefficient
mcq.zh: 感覺有效，但是最沒效率的方法之一。
mcq.en: It feels effective but is one of the least efficient ways.

mcq.q: What did Ebbinghaus discover?
options: People quickly forget new information without review
mcq.zh: 新資訊若不複習很快就會忘記。
mcq.en: People quickly forget new information unless they review it.

mcq.q: According to the passage, what makes a memory stronger?
mcq.en: Recalling something after a delay.

mcq.q: How do many language apps use the spacing effect?
options: They show words just before learners are likely to forget them
They show all words at once
mcq.zh: 在快要忘記之前再出現一次。
mcq.en: They show each word again just before the learner is likely to forget it.

mcq.q: The word "efficient" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
mcq.en: "Efficient" means productive without waste.

tf.s: Ebbinghaus was a German psychologist.
One long study session works better than several short reviews.
tf.en: False: spread-out reviews work far better.

tf.s: Ebbinghaus made his discovery in the 1980s.

s: In the early 1800s, moving goods across the United States was slow and costly.
Wagons on rough roads could carry only small loads.
paragraphs.zh: 十九世紀初，在美國境內運送貨物又慢又貴。在崎嶇道路上行駛的馬車只能載少量貨物。

s: In 1825, the state of New York completed the Erie Canal, a waterway about 580 kilometers long.
It connected the Hudson River with the Great Lakes.
paragraphs.zh: 1825 年，紐約州完成了伊利運河。這條水道長約五百八十公里，連接哈德遜河與五大湖。

s: Boats pulled by horses walking along the bank could carry heavy cargo at a fraction of the former cost.
Shipping prices dropped by about ninety percent.
paragraphs.zh: 由沿著河岸行走的馬匹拉動的船，能用過去一小部分的成本運送沉重的貨物。運費下降了大約九成。

s: The canal helped New York City become the country's leading port.
Within a few decades, however, railroads began to replace canals as the main way to move goods.
paragraphs.zh: 運河幫助紐約市成為全國首要的港口。然而不到幾十年，鐵路就開始取代運河，成為運送貨物的主要方式。

glossary.en: a river or canal boats use
goods carried by a ship or vehicle
a town where ships load and unload

mcq.q: What was the problem before the canal was built?
options: Moving goods was slow and costly
mcq.en: Moving goods was slow and costly.

mcq.q: What did the Erie Canal connect?
options: The Hudson River and the Great Lakes
mcq.zh: 連接哈德遜河與五大湖。
mcq.en: The Hudson River with the Great Lakes.

mcq.q: According to the passage, how were canal boats moved?
options: By horses walking along the bank
mcq.zh: 由沿岸行走的馬匹拉動。
mcq.en: They were pulled by horses walking along the bank.

mcq.q: What happened to shipping prices?
options: They fell by about ninety percent
mcq.en: They dropped by about ninety percent.

mcq.q: The word "fraction" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
mcq.en: "Fraction" means a small part.

tf.s: The Erie Canal was completed in 1825.
The canal made New York City less important.
tf.en: False: it made New York the leading port.

tf.s: Railroads later replaced canals as the main way to move goods.

title.zh: 睡眠中的大腦在做什麼

s: For centuries, sleep was seen as a time when the brain simply rested.
Modern research has shown that this view is wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 幾個世紀以來，睡眠一直被視為大腦單純休息的時間。現代研究已證明這種看法是錯的。

s: During sleep, the brain is busy sorting and storing the information gathered during the day.
Important memories are strengthened, while unimportant details are allowed to fade.
paragraphs.zh: 睡眠期間，大腦忙著整理並儲存白天收集到的資訊。重要的記憶會被強化，不重要的細節則任其淡去。

s: In experiments, people who slept after learning a task performed better the next day than those who stayed awake.
paragraphs.zh: 實驗中，學完一項任務後去睡覺的人，隔天的表現比整晚沒睡的人好。

s: Sleep also appears to clear waste products from the brain.
This may explain why long-term lack of sleep is linked to memory problems and illness.
paragraphs.zh: 睡眠似乎也能清除大腦中的廢物。這或許能解釋為什麼長期睡眠不足會和記憶問題及疾病有關。

glossary.en: something left over that the body does not need

mcq.q: What was the old view of sleep?
mcq.en: The brain simply rested.

mcq.q: What does the brain do with unimportant details during sleep?
mcq.en: It allows them to fade.

mcq.q: What did the experiments show?
options: Sleep has no effect on learning
mcq.zh: 睡過的人隔天表現較好。
mcq.en: People who slept performed better the next day.

mcq.q: According to the passage, what else does sleep appear to do?
options: Clear waste products from the brain
mcq.en: Clear waste products from the brain.

mcq.q: The word "fade" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
mcq.en: "Fade" means slowly disappear.

tf.s: Modern research agrees that the brain simply rests during sleep.
tf.en: False: research has shown this view is wrong.

tf.s: Long-term lack of sleep is linked to memory problems.
Important memories are strengthened during sleep.

items.text:
The Invention of the Printing Press
Before the fifteenth century, books in Europe were copied by hand. A single book could take months to produce, so books were rare and expensive, and few people outside churches and universities could read. Around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg developed a printing press that used movable metal type. Individual letters could be arranged to form a page, inked and pressed onto paper, and then rearranged for the next page.
The effects were dramatic. Within fifty years, millions of books had been printed across Europe. As books became cheaper, more people learned to read, and new ideas in science and religion spread far faster than before. Some historians argue that the printing press made possible the scientific revolution of the following centuries, because scientists could share and check one another's results.
Gutenberg himself did not become rich. He borrowed heavily to build his workshop, and a dispute with his business partner cost him much of his equipment.

tr.zh:
印刷機的發明
十五世紀以前，歐洲的書是手抄的。一本書可能要花幾個月才能完成，所以書既稀少又昂貴，教會和大學以外的人很少識字。大約 1450 年，古騰堡發展出使用活字金屬字模的印刷機。一個個字母可以排成一頁，上墨後壓印到紙上，再重新排列印下一頁。
影響十分巨大。五十年內，歐洲各地印了數百萬本書。書變便宜後，更多人學會識字，科學和宗教的新思想傳播得比以前快得多。有些歷史學家認為，印刷機促成了之後幾個世紀的科學革命，因為科學家能分享並檢驗彼此的成果。
古騰堡本人並沒有致富。他為了建工坊借了大筆錢，和生意夥伴的糾紛又讓他失去許多設備。

items.text:
How Cities Shape Bird Songs
Birds use songs to attract mates and defend territories, so it matters that other birds can hear them. In cities, however, songs must compete with traffic and construction noise, which is mostly low in pitch. Researchers studying great tits in several European cities found that urban birds sang at a higher pitch than birds of the same species in nearby forests.
One explanation is that higher notes are easier to hear above low-pitched noise. Some urban birds also sing louder, and others sing earlier in the morning, before traffic begins.
These changes may have costs. Female birds of some species prefer low-pitched songs, which may signal a larger, healthier male. A city male that sings higher may therefore be heard more easily but chosen less often. Scientists are still studying whether such changes are learned by young birds or are becoming part of their genes.

tr.zh:
城市如何改變鳥鳴
鳥用歌聲吸引配偶、保衛地盤，所以讓其他鳥聽得到很重要。但在城市裡，歌聲必須和交通、施工噪音競爭，而這些噪音大多是低音。研究人員觀察歐洲幾個城市的大山雀，發現城市裡的鳥比附近森林的同種鳥唱得更高。
一種解釋是高音比較容易在低沉的噪音中被聽見。有些城市鳥也唱得更大聲，有些則在交通開始前、更早的清晨唱歌。
這些改變可能有代價。有些鳥種的雌鳥偏好低音歌聲，因為那可能代表雄鳥較大、較健康。因此，唱得較高的城市雄鳥也許比較容易被聽到，卻比較少被選上。科學家仍在研究這些改變是幼鳥學來的，還是正成為基因的一部分。

items.text:
The Domestication of Wheat
About 10,000 years ago, people in the region known as the Fertile Crescent, in what is now the Middle East, began to grow wheat instead of only gathering it from the wild. This change was one of the most important steps in human history, because farming allowed people to stay in one place and build permanent villages.
Wild wheat has a problem for farmers: when its seeds are ripe, the head of the plant breaks apart and the seeds fall to the ground. This helps the plant spread, but it makes harvesting difficult. Occasionally, however, a plant had a mutation that kept its seeds attached. When early farmers harvested, they naturally collected more seeds from these plants and planted them the next year.
Over many generations, this unintentional selection produced wheat that kept its seeds until it was cut. Archaeologists can recognize domesticated wheat because the remains of its seed heads show a rough break, made by people threshing the grain, rather than the smooth break of wild wheat.

tr.zh:
小麥的馴化
大約一萬年前，在今日中東一帶稱為「肥沃月彎」的地區，人們開始種植小麥，而不只是從野外採集。這個改變是人類史上最重要的一步之一，因為農耕讓人們能定居一地，建立永久的村落。
野生小麥對農夫來說有個問題：種子成熟時，麥穗會散開，種子掉到地上。這有助於植物散播，卻讓收割很困難。不過偶爾會有植株發生突變，讓種子留在穗上。早期農夫收割時，自然會從這些植株收集到較多種子，隔年再種下。
經過許多世代，這種無意的選擇產生了收割前種子不會掉落的小麥。考古學家能辨認出馴化的小麥，因為其麥穗殘骸是人們脫粒造成的粗糙斷面，而不是野生小麥的平滑斷面。

items.text:
The Silk Road
The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes that connected China with Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe for more than 1,500 years. It takes its name from Chinese silk, which was highly valued in Rome, but many other goods traveled along it, including spices, glass, paper and horses.
Few merchants traveled the entire distance. Instead, goods usually passed through many hands, each trader carrying them part of the way before selling them to the next. As a result, prices rose steadily as goods moved west, and a piece of silk could be worth many times its original price by the time it reached the Mediterranean.
Perhaps even more important than the goods were the ideas that spread along the routes. Religions such as Buddhism traveled from India into China, and technologies such as papermaking moved westward. Historians therefore describe the Silk Road as one of the first examples of globalization.

tr.zh:
絲路
絲路不是一條路，而是一個貿易路線網絡，連接中國與中亞、中東和歐洲長達一千五百多年。它因中國絲綢而得名，絲綢在羅馬極受珍視，但沿路運送的還有許多其他貨物，包括香料、玻璃、紙和馬匹。
很少有商人走完全程。貨物通常經過許多人之手，每個商人只運一段路，再賣給下一個人。因此貨物往西走，價格就不斷上漲，一塊絲綢到達地中海時，可能值原價的好幾倍。
比貨物更重要的，或許是沿路傳播的思想。佛教等宗教從印度傳入中國，造紙等技術則往西傳。因此歷史學家把絲路形容為最早的全球化例子之一。
